ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a voltage-commutated chopper circuit; the left-side DC source is labeled V = 250 V; the upper main thyristor is labeled M; there is an auxiliary thyristor A in the middle; the left-side commutating capacitor is labeled 1 μF; the lower commutating inductor is labeled 2 mH; on the right side is a DC load with inductance and labeled with load current i_L, and beside it there is also a freewheeling diode branch. The problem statement gives the chopper operating frequency as 1 kHz, and the load current is assumed constant at 10 A. Reasoning: According to the minimum on-time requirement of the voltage-commutated chopper, the main SCR M must remain conducting until the commutating capacitor completes resonant voltage reversal. The time required for this resonant reversal is t_min = π√(LC). Substituting L = 2 mH = 2×10^-3 H, C = 1 μF = 1×10^-6 F gives √(LC) = √(2×10^-9) = 44.72 μs, therefore t_min = π × 44.72 μs ≈ 140.5 μs. The period of 1 kHz is 1000 μs, and 140 μs is less than this period, so the result is reasonable.

method.method_draft: First describe the image and identify that the auxiliary commutating branch has C = 1 μF and L = 2 mH around SCRs M and A. Use the text to note that the load current is assumed constant, so the load side can be treated as a current sink and the fast commutation-capacitor preparation is governed by the LC loop. Write the natural response of the initially charged capacitor in the LC loop: v_C(t) = V cos(t/√(LC)). planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Model the commutation branch as an ideal lossless series LC circuit initially charged to V. The capacitor voltage follows a cosine waveform, v_C(t) = V cos(ω0 t) with ω0 = 1/√(LC), and full reversal to -V occurs at ω0 t = π. Therefore the minimum permissible M conduction interval before a later commutation attempt is t = π/ω0 = π√(LC).
